stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: When the Halvorsen Viaduct opened in 1968, its designers expected the concrete deck to last about forty years before it would need full replacement. Road salt, repeated freeze-thaw cycles, and heavy truck traffic were all predicted to wear the deck down within that span. ______ a 2023 inspection found the deck still structurally sound, with corrosion limited to a few small patches near the drains.
explanation: The first two sentences set up an expectation: the deck should have worn out within about forty years. The sentence after the blank says something different. Fifty-five years later, the deck was still sound. The reality undercuts the prediction, so you need a contrast word, and "However" is the one that expresses it.

A.why: You treated the inspection result as an effect of the predicted wear. Salt, freezing, and traffic would lead you to expect damage, not a sound deck, so "Consequently" turns the logic upside down.

B.why: You saw that both sentences are about the deck's condition and picked an addition word without checking the direction of the logic. The inspection doesn't add to the prediction of wear. It contradicts it.

C.why: You read the inspection as one example of the predicted wear. It isn't a sample of what the designers expected. It shows the opposite.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Many shoppers assume that frozen vegetables lose much of their nutritional value and are a poor substitute for fresh produce. ______ when nutrition scientists compared frozen peas and spinach with fresh versions that had been refrigerated for five days, the frozen samples often contained as much vitamin C as the fresh ones or more, because freezing slows the breakdown of the vitamin.
explanation: The first sentence states a common belief: frozen vegetables are less nutritious. The sentence after the blank gives the measured fact that corrects that belief. When a mistaken assumption is followed by the truth, "Actually" is the word that marks the correction.

A.why: You noticed that the second sentence contains a cause (freezing slows vitamin loss) and reached for a cause-and-effect word. The finding isn't a result of what shoppers assume. It overturns it.

C.why: You matched the two sentences because both are about frozen versus fresh vegetables. "Similarly" says the second idea runs in the same direction as the first, but the study contradicts the shoppers' belief.

D.why: You treated the study as a more precise restatement of the first sentence. "Specifically" zooms in on the same claim, but this sentence argues against that claim instead of sharpening it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Ornithologists have documented many remarkable abilities in the bar-tailed godwit. Before migrating, the shorebird can nearly double its body weight by storing fat, and it can shrink its digestive organs to save weight during travel. It also appears to time its departures to catch favorable winds. ______ none of these abilities rivals its nonstop flight from Alaska to New Zealand, a journey of more than 11,000 kilometers.
explanation: The passage lists several impressive abilities. The sentence after the blank then turns against that list and ranks one feat above all of them. That turn calls for a concession: the other abilities are remarkable, but the nonstop flight beats them. "Still" marks that turn.

A.why: You noticed that fat storage and organ shrinking help make the long flight possible, so you read the sentence as a result. But the sentence isn't saying the flight happens because of those abilities. It is saying the flight outranks them, and that is a contrast.

B.why: This is the trap. Because every sentence praises the godwit, you assumed the last one continues in the same direction. In fact, it sets one feat above the others. "Similarly" can't introduce a sentence that says "none of these abilities rivals" something.

D.why: You treated the final sentence as a restatement of the list. It introduces a new feat and ranks it above everything listed, so it isn't saying the same thing in other words.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: After three unusually dry summers, agronomist Lena Marsh advised farmers in the Corrigan Valley to replace their corn with drought-tolerant sorghum, expecting the dry pattern to continue. Several growers followed her recommendation. ______ the next growing season brought the heaviest rainfall the valley had recorded in decades, and the farmers who had kept planting corn harvested their best yields in ten years.
explanation: Marsh's advice rested on an expectation: the dry weather would continue. The sentence after the blank reports the opposite. Record rain fell, and the farmers who ignored her advice did best. Reality went against the expectation, so "However" is the logical transition.

A.why: You treated the record rainfall as a consequence of Marsh's advice or of the farmers following it. Nothing in the passage connects them causally. The rain is an unexpected turn, not an outcome of the advice.

B.why: You saw that both sentences are about the valley's weather and crops and picked an addition word. The heavy rain doesn't add to Marsh's forecast of continued drought. It contradicts it.

C.why: You read the rainy season as an example of something in the first sentences. It doesn't illustrate the advice or the dry pattern. It overturns the expectation behind them.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: For decades, sprint coaches told athletes to hold long static stretches before a race, assuming that looser muscles would produce faster starts. ______ when sports scientist Lena Ortiz timed 40 college sprinters, those who had held static stretches ran a 30-meter dash slightly slower than those who had warmed up by jogging.
explanation: The first sentence states what coaches assumed: stretching makes sprinters faster. The second reports what Ortiz found: stretched sprinters were slower. Sentence two is the opposite of what sentence one leads you to expect, so you need a concession word. 'However' signals that reversal.

B.why: You noticed that both sentences are about stretching and sprinting, and you didn't check which way the logic runs. 'For this reason' says the coaches' belief caused the slower times. The study tested the belief and contradicted it. It was not a result of the belief.

C.why: 'Similarly' says the second sentence matches the first. The study doesn't support the coaches' assumption. It undercuts it.

D.why: 'For instance' introduces a case that illustrates the previous claim. Ortiz's result doesn't illustrate the idea that stretching speeds up starts. It shows the opposite.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Stainless steel owes its reputation to chromium, which forms a thin oxide film that shields the iron beneath it. Many builders therefore assume the metal cannot corrode at all. ______ in salty coastal air, chloride ions can break through the film, leaving small pits in railings and fasteners.
explanation: The second sentence reports a mistaken belief: stainless steel never corrodes. The third gives the true fact that it can corrode in salty air. When a belief is followed by the fact that corrects it, a correction word like 'in reality' fits best.

A.why: The passage describes how the oxide film works, so you expected an outcome of that mechanism. But the pitting doesn't result from the builders' assumption. It proves the assumption wrong. 'As a result' wrongly claims a cause.

B.why: You saw that both sentences discuss stainless steel and corrosion and picked an addition word. The pitting doesn't add to the claim that the metal can't corrode. It contradicts that claim.

D.why: 'For example' would make the coastal pitting a sample of the builders' belief. It is a counterexample to that belief, not an illustration of it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Fossil pollen has helped paleobotanists date lake sediments, trace the spread of ancient grasslands, and estimate past rainfall. ______ pollen grains are rarely enough to identify the exact species of plant that shed them, because many related plants produce grains that look nearly identical under a microscope.
explanation: The first sentence lists what fossil pollen does well. The second names an important limit on what it can do. A list of successes followed by a shortcoming calls for a concession word. 'Still' grants the successes and then turns against them.

A.why: 'Therefore' claims that the pollen's usefulness causes the identification problem. The usefulness doesn't cause the limit. The limit holds in spite of it.

B.why: This is the trap. You read a string of achievements and expected one more, so you reached for an addition word. Sentence two is a weakness, not another strength, so it pivots against the list.

C.why: 'For instance' would make the second sentence one of the uses just listed. A limitation isn't an example of a success.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: When the city of Harlow Falls launched a free bike-share program, health officials hoped it would raise daily exercise levels in the city's lowest-income neighborhoods. ______ a two-year survey found that most riders lived in wealthier districts near downtown stations, while use in the targeted neighborhoods stayed low.
explanation: The first sentence states a hope: the program would help low-income neighborhoods. The second reports that it mostly reached wealthier riders. That outcome is the reverse of the hope, so you need a concession word. 'However' is the only choice that signals the reversal.

A.why: 'Consequently' says the officials' hope produced the survey results. A hope doesn't cause low ridership. The results simply failed to match it.

C.why: This is the trap. Both sentences are about the bike-share program, so an addition word seemed safe. But the survey doesn't build on the officials' hope. It reports that the hope wasn't met.

D.why: 'Specifically' restates the previous sentence more precisely. The survey findings don't zoom in on the hope. They contradict it.

stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
stimulus: Because English spells the same sound in many different ways, as in "though," "throw," and "sew," many learners assume that its spelling follows no rules at all. ______ linguists have shown that most English spellings become predictable once a reader takes into account a word's origin and its relationship to other words.
explanation: The first sentence gives a mistaken belief: English spelling has no rules. The second gives the true fact that most spellings are predictable. When sentence one is a belief and sentence two corrects it, 'actually' fits best.

A.why: The first sentence opens with 'because', so you may have expected a conclusion to follow. But the linguists' finding isn't a result of the learners' assumption. It overturns that assumption, so 'thus' sets up a false cause.

C.why: 'Similarly' says the linguists agree with the learners. They don't. The learners think spelling has no rules, and the linguists show that it mostly does.

D.why: 'For example' would make the linguists' finding an illustration of spelling having no rules. The finding argues against that idea, so it can't serve as an example of it.
